title: If you have time
goal: Say what will happen if something happens, with -sA.

intro.text: Add `-sA` and a past ending to the verb for **if**: *gelsem* (if I come), *gelseň* (if you come), *gelse* (if he comes). The **if** half comes first: *Wagtyň bolsa, gel* (come if you have time). *Eger* (if) in front is optional.

exercises.question: How do you say **if I come**?

why.1: *Gelsin* means **let him come**: that is `-sYn`, not `-sA`.

exercises.label: *okamak* + `-sA`: if I read, if you read…
exercises.explain: Back vowel a: *-sa*, then the past endings *-m, -ň*, nothing, *-k, -ňyz, -lar*.

exercises.en: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay at home.

reject.why: *Ýagýar* is **it's raining**. For **if it rains**, use `-sA`: *ýagsa*.

exercises.explain: *ýag-* + *-sa*: if it rains. The main verb *galarys* says what will follow.

reject.why: The **you** is already in *wagtyň* (your time). *Bolsa* stays in the third person: *Wagtyň bolsa*.
That says **you have time, come**: no if. Add `-sA` to *bol-*: *Wagtyň bolsa, gel*.

exercises.explain: *wagtyň* (your time) + *bolsa* (if it is): if you have time. Then the order *gel*.

accept: If it does not rain, we will go to the park.
If it does not rain, we [are going to go|are going] to the park.
We will go to the park if it does not rain.
If there is no rain, we will go to the park.
If it does not rain, we will go to a park.

exercises.question: *Wagtym bolsa, kitap okaýaryn.* What does it mean?
options: When I have time, I read.
If I had time, I would read.
I had time, so I read.

why.1: **I would read** needs `-ArdY`: *okardym*. *Okaýaryn* is what usually happens.

exercises.explain: With `-ýAr` in the main clause, `-sA` means **whenever**: when I have time, I read.
*git-* keeps its t before a consonant: *git-* + *-se* + *-k* (we).

exercises.prompt: If you come to Ashgabat, call me.
Hurry up, or else we'll be late.
accept: Çalt bol, ýogsa biz gijä galarys.
[Çalt bol|Howluk|Çalt boluň|Howlukyň], ýogsa biz gijä galjak.

reject.why: *Galjak* has no ending, so it needs its subject: *ýogsa biz gijä galjak*, or *galarys*.

exercises.explain: *Ýogsa* means **otherwise**: if we don't hurry. *Gijä galmak* is **to be late**.

exercises.question: Your friend looks tired. What do you say to suggest a break?

why.1: *Alsyn* is **let him rest**, about someone else.
why.2: *Aldyň* is **you rested**: a past, not a suggestion.

exercises.explain: `-sA` on its own with a question mark is a gentle suggestion: how about a little rest?

accept: If it is possible, (please) come tomorrow morning.
If possible, please come tomorrow morning.
[Please come|Come] tomorrow morning if (it is) possible.
If (it is) possible, (please) come in the morning tomorrow.

exercises.en: If the weather is warm, we'll go to the lake.

reject.why: The **if** half is about the weather, *howa*: third person, no ending: *bolsa*.

exercises.explain: *Howa ýyly bolsa* (if the weather is warm), then the future *gideris* (we'll go).

exercises.prompt: If I see Merdan, I'll tell him.
exercises.explain: *Merdany* (Merdan, as the object) + *görsem* (if I see), then *oňa aýdaryn* (I'll tell him).
